title: Oldest modern human genomes yet date Neanderthal mixing
place: Ranis, Germany, and Zlatý kůň, Czechia
summary: Genomes from seven people who lived 49,000-42,000 years ago narrowed the main interbreeding with Neanderthals to about 49,000-45,000 years ago, later than earlier estimates.
why: Tightens the clock on when our ancestors left Africa and met Neanderthals.

notes.problem: Source states 'oldest genomes of modern humans to date' plainly; the superlative is time-bound, so mark it 'yet'.

superlativeSource: decoding the oldest genomes of modern humans to date
